key_insight: A GPU-accelerated LBM-LES pipeline can reconstruct near-real-time, meter-scale 3D urban wind fields from sparse observations in complex city geometry.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, physics-based wind nowcasting for low-altitude micrometeorology and flight safety in dense urban environments.
method: High-fidelity urban morphology reconstruction that explicitly resolves building details
Observation-driven boundary assimilation into a rapid LBM-LES simulation pipeline
GPU acceleration to produce kilometer-scale, 5 m-resolution 3D wind fields within minutes
evidence_signal: Validated with multi-site Doppler lidar data in dense urban Guangzhou, including withheld-station tests, observation reduction experiments, and grid/precursor sensitivity analyses.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy may depend on lidar availability, grid resolution, and precursor-domain extent, so deployment needs careful local tuning.
paper_title: Near-real-time, meter-scale 3D urban wind modeling for low-altitude micrometeorology: numerical verification of a GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann framework
